Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Australian opening pair of Travis Head and skipper Aaron Finch is at the middle. Shaheen Afridi has the ball in hand and he is ready to steam in. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! Australia need 163 runs to win and from what we have seen from this surface in the ODI series, it should not be a difficult chase by any means. Pakistan though have a lot of firepower with the ball and will be in search of early wickets. One final innings before the tour ends and neither team will back down. The exciting run chase coming up.

The Australian dressing room will be mightily pleased with that bowling effort. They have a young pace attack but apart from Ben Dwarshuis who had an outing to forget on debut, everyone else was just right on the money. T20I debutant Cameron Green got the visitors going with a double whammy in his first over and the experienced Sean Abbott and Adam Zampa kept the scoring rate in check. It was then young Nathan Ellis, who seems to be going from strength to strength, and after being hit for 14 runs in his first over made a statement with a four-wicket haul to rock the opposition.

After a thunderous start with the bat, Pakistan were rocked by a double-blow by Cameron Green in the 8th over and from there everything seemed to go downhill. Babar Azam looked in fine form to start with but as the wickets kept tumbling, his scoring rate went down. Azam did get to yet another half century but fell soon after. Apart from Khushdil Shah, no other batter in the Pakistani middle-order could muster up runs and it was a spirited cameo in the final over by Usman Qadir that has taken Pakistani to a sort of a defendable score.

Top drawer stuff from the Aussie bowlers but that last over from Ben Dwarshuis has spoiled things a bit. Still, they have done extremely well to restrict Pakistan to a score of just 162 runs which truth be told is well below par on this surface. The key to this successful bowling display was the regularity with which the Aussies picked up wickets and after the opening partnership never allowed another stand to brew.
Ben Dwarshuis goes very full and around off, Usman Qadir nails his drive through covers and scampers back for the second run. 18 from the final over, Pakistan end on 162/8!

MISFIELD AND FOUR! The crowd is making a lot of noise. Back of a length, around off, Qadir rocks back and hammers it over mid-wicket. Marnus Labuschagne scoots to his right, tries to pick it on the bounce but it bursts through his palms and goes for a boundary.
Yorker outside off, Wasim digs it out down to long off for a run.
Too full and wide outside off, Usman squeezes it out to backward point for a single.
SIX! Usman Qadir shows his batting muscle. Fuller and on off, Usman Qadir swings his bat across the line and hoists it over mid-wicket for a biggie. 150 comes up!
What happened there? Not sure, the umpires are in conversation with the reserve umpire about something. Anyway, the play resumes...
FOUR! Vital runs! Delivers it on a length, around off, Usman Qadir rocks back and powers it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Ben Dwarshuis to bowl the last over.
Slower one, on a length and outside off, Usman pushes it through covers for a single. 4-0-28-4, fantastic from Ellis.
Slower again, very full and on off, Wasim keeps it out from the toe end of the bat to the leg side for a run.
Slower one, full and outside off, Wasim pushes at it early and misses.

Huge shout for a caught behind! The finger stays down. Aaron Finch smiles and takes the DRS. A touch short in length and close to off, Wasim rocks back to punch it through the line but misses. There is some noise as it goes to the keeper and they appeal. The UltraEdge finds no wood and the noise was of the bat clipping the flap of the back pad.
Usman Qadir is the number 10 batter.

OUT! BRILLIANTLY CAUGHT! Beautiful slower one, on a length and outside off at 113.4 kph, Shaheen throws his bat at it and gets a big top edge towards covers. Marcus Stoinis sprints across to his left from point, keeps his eyes on the ball as he stretches to grab it with both hands. The ball pops out initially as he goes down but he does well to snap it with his right hand. The umpires quickly get it checked upstairs and it's a clean catch. It's a procession for Pakistan. Nathan Ellis is on a hat-trick...
Commentary.Howout: c Marcus Stoinis b Nathan Ellis

Commentary.Commentary: Mohammad Wasim is the new batter.

OUT! Shah departs and it's a big blow! The crowd is silenced once again. A low full toss around off at 136.8 kph, Khushdil tries to clear long on with the big extension of his arms but fails to give it enough power. The ball flies from the lower half of his blade and Ben McDermott takes a sitter in the deep.
Commentary.Howout: c Ben McDermott b Nathan Ellis

Commentary.Commentary: Short in length and on off, at 133 clicks, Shaheen defends it from the back foot. 4-0-28-1, Sean is done for the evening with the ball.
Shaheen Afridi is in next.

OUT! Chops it on! Sean Abbott takes his revenge. Fires in a yorker outside off at 140.7 kph, Hasan steps back and tries to squeeze it out but it takes the inner edge and goes on to rattle the stumps. End of a short cameo from Hasan!
FOUR! That's clever! Full toss, outside off, Hasan walks across the stumps and paddles it wide of short fine leg for a boundary. The crowd roars.
SIX! Dismissed! This one is on a length, around off and slower in pace, Hasan reads the pace early and launches it over the sightscreen for a biggie.
Short in length and outside off, at 119 clicks, Hasan Ali tries to pull but is early into the shot.
Yorker on middle, Shah digs it out down to mid on for a run.
Caught off a no ball! High full toss on middle, Shah heaves it over mid-wicket and is caught in the deep. The umpire calls it a no ball and the batters have taken a couple. Free Hit will follow...
Change! Sean Abbott is ready to bowl his final over.
Fuller and on middle, forced down to long on for a single. Top over!

Appeal for an lbw, the finger has gone up! Looks to be going down the leg side and Khushdil Shah takes the review. Nathan Ellis steams in from 'round the wicket and angles in a length ball on middle at 129.8 kph. Shah tries to flick but misses and is rapped on the front pad. The Ball Tracking finds that it's missing the leg stump and the crowd rejoices.
Hasan Ali walks in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! The big hitter is gone without doing any damage. Clever bowling from Nathan Ellis. He takes the pace off this delivery and lands it full around middle at 107.8 kph. Asif Afridi finds it in his range and attempts to power it into the stand at deep mid-wicket. He though gets more height than distance and Marnus Labuschagne secures the catch safely in the deep.
Commentary.Howout: c Marnus Labuschagne b Nathan Ellis

Commentary.Commentary: Spears it in very full and on middle at 137.9 kph, Shah tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto the boot. It deflects to the off side and they cross.
FOUR! Finds the gap! Full toss, around middle and off, Khushdil accepts the gift gleefully and heaves it in front of square on the leg side for a one-bounce boundary.
Delivers it on a good length and around off, Asif punches it to extra cover for a run.
Nathan Ellis is back on for his third over.
Fires it full and on the pads, Asif clips it to deep mid-wicket for a run. 4-0-29-1, Zampa is done.
Loopy one, full and on off, pushed straight to short cover.
Down the leg side, nudged to short fine leg for a single.
Slower through the air, full and outside off, Asif drives it aerially but wide of the bowler and down to long off for a run.
Asif Ali is the new batter.

OUT! Babar holes out! Stunned silence in the stadium! Smart bowling from the leggie. He tosses it up and lands it full and wide outside off. Babar has to reach out for it as he attempts for a lofted shot over covers. Doesn't get the timing right and it's a simple catch for Nathan Ellis. A body blow for Pakistan as they lose a set batter at this stage of the match.
Commentary.Howout: c Nathan Ellis b Adam Zampa

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! High and handsome! Zampa serves it quicker through the air, around middle and leg, Babar clears his front leg and clobbers it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Adam Zampa is back into the attack. 0 for 20 in his 2 overs so far.
Excellent delivery to end the over! Yorker, at the base of the off pole and Khushdil Shah can only jam it out towards the bowler.
Full and straight, Babar Azam heaves it down towards wide long on and collects a single. Azam is struggling to find the boundary at the moment.
Very full again, outside off. Shah reaches out and gets it off the toe end towards long off. Single taken.

FOUR! Miss the mark and you will be punished! Abbott misses the yorker and serves a low full toss around the pads. Shah heaves it through mid-wicket and beats the diving fielder at the fence. A much-needed boundary for Pakistan.
Dot ball and the pressure keeps on mounting. Sean Abbott finds the blockhole and this one tails away from the left-hander as well. Khushdil Shah manages to dig it out.
Very full, at the base of middle and leg. Babar Azam makes a bit of room by moving on the leg side and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Another excellent over from the big man, just four singles off it. Pitched up and slanted into middle. Shah punches it back to the bowler.
Change in bowling. Sean Abbott (2-0-7-0) to bowl his third.
Quick single this time. Around off, dabbed down to backward point for one.
Firmly hit for no run! Around off and Babar Azam crunches the drive straight to the man at extra cover.
Shorter in length, slower and outside off. Shah only manages to tap it towards deep point for a single.
Good-length this time, over middle. Babar Azam hangs back and pushes it through mid on for just another single.
Back of a length, around off. Shah steers it behind point for a single.
Cameron Green (2 for 12 in 2 overs) is back on.
Around off, worked towards mid-wicket for a run.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single by Babar. The 100 is up for Pakistan.
Short and wide again, Shah misses out as he only manages to tap it in front of square on the off side for a single.
FOUR! Edgy boundary but Khushdil Shah won't mind. This is angled into middle and leg. Shah looks for the slog but gets an inside edge past the leg stump and the ball runs away to the fine leg fence.
Short and wide this time, Shah cuts but finds the man at backward point.
This is angled into off from 'round the wicket. Shah dabs it down on the off side.
Travis Head is back on. His first over went for 10 runs.

Ellis comes from 'round the wicket to the left-hander and serves a yorker-length ball on middle. Khushdil Shah blocks it out towards wide mid on for a quick single. Great comeback over, 5 runs and a wicket off it!
Khushdil Shah is the new batter.

OUT! TAKEN! Nathan Ellis comes back stronger and gets a wicket! Ellis just pitches it a bit further up and outside off. The ball is there to be hit but Iftikhar Ahmed doesn't go hard at it. Ahmed tries to drive away from the body and looks to caress it through covers. The ball just shapes away a bit and takes the outside edge. Josh Inglis springs to his right and takes a fine catch. Just when a partnership was blossoming, Pakistan lose another wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Josh Inglis b Nathan Ellis

Commentary.Commentary: Around the top of off, a bit of a heave from Babar Azam, in front of square on the leg side, and it will only be another single.
These two just trying to build a partnership here and not taking any unwanted risks at the moment. Slower delivery, on off and Ahmed nudges it out to cover-point for one.
Full and on off, Babar punches it uppishly down to long off and rotates the strike.
Length ball on off. This is hit on the up and through extra cover for a run.
Nathan Ellis is back on. He went for 14 runs in his only over so far.
This is pushed wider and Ahmed strokes it along the ground towards sweeper cover for a single. 9 from this over!
Zampa sees Azam advancing and spears it in at the batter's toes. Azam manages to clip it through mid-wicket for a run.
On off, Ahmed turns it through mid on for a single. Smart batting, just keeping the scoreboard ticking after the boundary.
FOUR! Finds the gap does Iftikhar Ahmed. Tossed up from Zampa and ends up being a juicy full toss on off. Ahmed drives it past the man at extra cover and picks up a boundary.
Bit of width outside off and this is tapped towards deep cover for one more.
Zampa drags it down around middle and leg and bowls it quicker as well. Ahmed half-pulls it towards deep backward square leg for a run.
Short ball, around off, Iftikhar Ahmed pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run. 8 from the over, Pakistan are 80/2 at the halfway mark!
Fuller and on middle, eased to deep square leg for a run.

FOUR! Easy pickings! On a length and around leg, angling down, Babar picks it off his pads and deflects it wide of short fine leg for a boundary. FIFTY FOR BABAR, his 26th in this format and he raises his bat to acknowledge the crowd. What a consistent player across formats!
Very full and around leg, sliding down, Ahmed tries to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to backward square and they cross. The bowler appeals but nothing doing. A leg bye added to the total.
Keeps it full and the line is on middle and leg, Babar flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller in length and around off, Babar strokes it through the line and the short cover fielder makes a running stop to his right.
Tossed up, full and on off, knocked down to long on for a run. A very good over by the leggie.

IN THE AIR... Lands safely! Short and on off, turning away, Babar goes back to cut but it takes the top edge and flies towards backward point. It doesn't carry to Mitchell Swepson who is on the field for Aaron Finch. The Aussie skipper has hurt his fingers while taking the catch.
Quicker through the air, full and on leg, Iftikhar Ahmed flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Googly around off, a bit on the shorter side, Ahmed punches it off the back foot but the short mid-wicket fielder makes a running stop to his left.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Babar drives it down to long off and rotates the strike.
Flighted leg spinner, full and outside off, Ahmed slices his drive wide of short third man for a single.
No hat-trick! Back of a length, on off, Ahmed punches it to the right of point and gets off the mark with a single. Top over, 5 runs and two wickets off it!
Iftikhar Ahmed walks in next at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT! Fakhar Zaman stands there in shock. Green greets him with a full toss, around off at 118.5 kph, Fakhar tries to heave it over the leg side but only manages to drag it off the bottom half to mid on. It goes uppishly to the fielder and Aaron Finch is not dropping those. Cameron Green is on a hat-trick...
Commentary.Howout: c Aaron Finch b Cameron Green

Commentary.Commentary: Fakhar Zaman walks in next.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Cameron Green strikes to get the breakthrough and also his maiden T20I wicket. Lovely deception from the big man. He rolls his fingers over the ball and serves a cutter outside off at 121.3 kph. It lands just outside off, Mohammad Rizwan shuffles across a bit to flick but misses and it perhaps takes a bit of inside edge before going on to demolish the stumps. Green is pumped up and a disappointed Rizwan returns.

Physio comes out. Mohammad Rizwan does seem a bit uncomfortable out there and the last couple of balls haven't made it any easier. The physio applies some magic spray and the players take this opportunity to take a breather as well. A new pair of gloves is being brought out for Babar Azam as Rizwan continues to receive treatment. Finally, Rizwan is back on his feet and we are good to continue.

A low full toss on middle, Rizwan nudges it to deep mid-wicket and again limps to complete the second run. He is in some pain here. Perhaps the inside edge that hit him on the pads in the previous over is bothering him.
Full and on middle, Rizwan flicks it through square leg and hobbles back for the second run. He is feeling some discomfort with his left leg.
Starts well. A yorker outside off, Rizwan digs it out back to the bowler.
Cameron Green, on his T20I debut, is introduced into the attack.
Flatter and on middle, tucked to deep square leg for a run. 7 from Zampa's first.
Miscues again! Zampa drags his length back, around off, Rizwan goes back to pull but gets an inside edge onto the pads.

Quicker through the air, full and on middle, Rizwan walks forward to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It deflects to short third man and he looks for a run but is sent back. Australia appealed momentarily.
Loopy delivery, full and around off, Babar opens the face of his blade and drives it to sweeper cover for a run.
FOUR! Quicker through the air, short in length and on middle, Babar goes on the back foot and pulls it with power through wide mid on. It beats the fielder near the fence and goes for a boundary.
Floated and full, around off, Rizwan draws forward and wrists it through mid-wicket for a single.
Change in bowling. Adam Zampa to roll his arm.
Fuller and around leg, it's eased wide of mid on for a couple of runs. 16 from the over. End of the Powerplay, Pakistan are 56/0!
SIX! Babar has nailed that and the crowd is loving it! Full and around off, Babar steps back to give himself room and lofts it nonchalantly over wide long off for a biggie. 50 up for Pakistan!
Digs it in short again, on off, it's pulled to deep square leg for a single.
FOUR! Not from the middle! Short and wide outside off, Rizwan tries to cut but it takes the bottom edge and speeds past the keeper for a boundary at third man.
Slightly short again, around off, Babar heaves it over square leg for a run.
Ben delivers it short and on middle, Babar walks forward and helps it to mid-wicket for a run. The fielder has a necessary shy at the striker's end and misses. They get two.
Ben Dwarshuis to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.
Uppish but safe! Pitched up, outside off. Babar tries to drag it over mid-wicket but mistimes it towards wide mid on and picks up a single.
A bit of away shape again. This is the knuckle-ball from Sean Abbott, full and around off. The ball shapes away from Rizwan who whips it through mid-wicket for one more.
This is full and angling into middle. Azam stands tall and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full again, around off and this is jammed out towards the cover region.

This one swung a bit in the air. Fullish delivery, around off and Babar Azam advances but he has to check his shot due to the movement in the air. Does well to defend it in the end back towards the bowler.
Abbott goes wide of off stump and bowls it slower. Rizwan pushes it towards extra cover and picks up a single.
Slower length ball, on off. Rizwan waits for it and nudges it behind square on the leg side for a run. 14 off the over and Pakistan are off to a flier!
On off, eased down to long off for a single this time.
FOUR! A bit too straight from Nathan Ellis and he's been hit for three boundaries on the trot! Down the leg side, it's flicked down wide of short fine leg by Babar Azam.
FOUR! The ball has rocketed to the fence! It's the change up this time from Ellis and it is angled into the body. Babar Azam heaves it over mid-wicket and picks up another boundary.
FOUR! Not perfectly timed but it's timed well enough. Short of a length, Azam swings through the line and clears mid on with ease. He picks up another boundary.
Hitting the top of off and Babar Azam winds up for the big shot. The ball comes off the splice of the bat and goes towards mid on.
Nathan Ellis to bowl the next over.
Top over from Sean Abbott! Full and outside off, just a bit of movement in the air. Rizwan looks to flick it on the leg side but ends up blocking it back to the bowler.
Length again, a bit wider and this is driven on the up. There is a fielder placed at deep cover and it will only be a single for Babar Azam this time.
Length, on off and Babar Azam gets right behind the line to make the block.
This is pitched up on middle and Azam uses the bottom hand to swat it through the mid-wicket region. He picks up a couple of runs.
Around off, driven straight to the man at cover.

Appeal for an lbw! Not given. A bit high maybe. Sean Abbott is on the money from the get-go. Fuller length, around off and nipping back in. Mohammad Rizwan gets caught on the crease and gets pinged on the pads. The ball rolls onto the leg side and they scamper through for a leg bye.
It was a decent first over by Head until the last ball. Will Aaron Finch stick with the part-timer? The answer is no. Here comes Sean Abbott...

Good hustle from Nathan Ellis in the deep. It's pitched up and slanted across the right-hander. Babar Azam leans into the cover drive and gets it well in front of square. Ellis runs around from the point fence and keeps it down to a couple.
Around the top of off, Azam punches it out off the back foot.
Just short of a length, around leg. Rizwan half-pulls it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Quick single! Fuller this time and Azam firmly pushes it towards mid on for a single.
On a good length, around off. Azam tucks it away towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Ben Dwarshuis's first ball in international cricket is greeted with a boundary. Length ball, just a bit of width outside off and Babar Azam is onto it in a flash. Azam hangs back and slaps it behind point for a boundary.
Who will bowl from the opposite end? It's going to be the debutant, Ben Dwarshuis.

SIX! Here we go! Mohammad Rizwan wasn't going to let the part-timer off the hook so easily. On middle again and this is slogged away over the mid-wicket fence for the first maximum of the innings. 10 off the first over!
On leg, Babar pushes it down the ground for yet another single.
Yet another single down to long on. This is very full, around middle and leg. Rizwan drills it towards long on for a run.
On middle, driven through mid on for a single and Babar Azam is off the mark as well.
Babar Azam will feel he missed out. This is floated wide of off stump and Azam slaps it straight to the man at cover.
Head starts from 'round the wicket and bowls it full on middle. Mohammad Rizwan is off the mark straightaway with a wristy drive down to long on for a single.

It's time to get underway! The Aussies are taking the field. The crowd has been very vocal. Out come Mohammad Rizwan and Babar Azam to open for Pakistan. Aaron Finch is beginning with the part-time spin of Travis Head. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the match! But first, the two sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Robert Key is pitchside and informs that it's the same surface that was used during the second ODI. He says that batting first or second won't matter much as it is a lovely batting surface but the spinners might have a say. Adds that there is a bit of dew but not that much and 180 is a minimum requisite batting first.

Australia (Playing XI) - Aaron Finch (C), Travis Head, Josh Inglis (WK), Marnus Labuschagne (On T20I debut), Marcus Stoinis, Cameron Green (On T20I debut), Ben McDermott, Sean Abbott, Ben Dwarshuis (On debut), Nathan Ellis and Adam Zampa.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Fakhar Zaman, Iftikhar Ahmed, Khushdil Shah, Asif Ali, Mohammad Wasim, Hasan Ali, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf and Usman Qadir.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it lands in Australia's favour. They have elected to BOWL first.

Babar Azam and his troops are currently enjoying a purple patch and they will be charged up for one final match in this tour. The hosts were ever so dominant in last year's T20 World Cup but faltered in the semis and coincidentally it was Australia who ended their hopes then. They have become a top T20 side and will look to hand their opponents a third defeat in a row on this tour and get a bit of revenge for that semi-final loss as well. So, will the Aussies be able to end the tour on a high? Or will the hosts take bragging rights? We'll find out soon. Toss and team sheets in a bit.

Australia are the reigning World T20 Champions but will have to field a very different side to the one that featured regularly in that tournament due to the unavailability of their star players. The visitors still have a plethora of talent in their ranks and skipper Aaron Finch will be looking to turn a new leaf and lead from the front tonight against a rejuvenated Pakistani team.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final match of Australia's tour of Pakistan and we end the tour with a one-off T20I contest. Two teams who have been dominant in this format in the last year or so go head-to-head in the shortest format of the game at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore and a tasty encounter is on the cards.
... MATCH DAY ...
